content: The references provided are a comprehensive list of studies, reviews, and guidelines related to tuberculosis (TB) and HIV, focusing on prevention, treatment, and management strategies. 1. Zunza M, Gray DM, Young T, Cotton M, Zar HJ conducted a systematic review to evaluate the efficacy of isoniazid in preventing tuberculosis in children infected with HIV. Their findings were published in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2017. 2. Zenner D, Beer N, Harris RJ, Lipman MC, Stagg HR, and van der Werf MJ performed an updated network meta-analysis to assess the treatment of latent tuberculosis infection. Their work was published in the Annals of Internal Medicine in 2017. 3. Comstock GW explored the optimal dosage of isoniazid required for tuberculosis prevention in immunocompetent adults. This study was published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 1999. 4. Stagg HR, Zenner D, Harris RJ, Muñoz L, Lipman MC, and Abubakar I conducted a network meta-analysis on the treatment of latent tuberculosis infection, with their findings published in the Annals of Internal Medicine in 2014. 5. The World Health Organization (WHO) released guidelines on the management of latent tuberculosis infection, accessible through their online repository as of September 27, 2023. 6. Diallo T, Adjibiméy M, Ruslami R, Trajman A, Sow O, Obeng Baah J, et al. compared the safety and side effects of rifampin versus isoniazid in children. Their findings were published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2018. 7. Menzies D, Dion MJ, Rabinovitch B, Mannix S, Brassard P, and Schwartzman K conducted a randomized trial comparing the completion rates and costs of a 4-month rifampin regimen versus a 9-month isoniazid regimen for latent tuberculosis infection. This study was published in the American Journal of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine in 2004. 8. WHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis, specifically Module 6, address tuberculosis and comorbidities. These guidelines are available online as of September 27, 2023. 9. Menzies D, Long R, Trajman A, Dion MJ, Yang J, Al Jahdali H, et al. investigated adverse events associated with 4 months of rifampin therapy versus 9 months of isoniazid therapy for latent tuberculosis infection in a randomized trial. Their findings were published in the Annals of Internal Medicine in 2008. 10. Swindells S, Ramchandani R, Gupta A, Benson CA, Leon-Cruz J, Mwelase N, et al. evaluated the efficacy of a 1-month regimen of rifapentine plus isoniazid for preventing HIV-related tuberculosis. This study was published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2019. 11. Martinson NA, Barnes GL, Moulton LH, Msandiwa R, Hausler H, Ram M, et al. examined new regimens for preventing tuberculosis in adults with HIV infection. Their findings were published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2011. 12. Sterling TR, Villarino ME, Borisov AS, Shang N, Gordin F, Bliven-Sizemore E, et al. assessed the efficacy of a 3-month regimen of rifapentine and isoniazid for latent tuberculosis infection. This study was published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2011. 13. Sterling TR, Scott NA, Miró JM, Calvet G, La Rosa A, Infante R, et al. investigated the use of a 3-month weekly regimen of rifapentine and isoniazid for treating Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection in HIV-coinfected individuals. Their findings were published in AIDS in 2016. 14. Villarino ME, Scott NA, Weis SE, Weiner M, Conde MB, Jones B, et al. conducted a randomized clinical trial to evaluate a 3-month, 12-dose regimen of rifapentine and isoniazid for preventing tuberculosis in children and adolescents. This study was published in JAMA Pediatrics in 2015. 15. Den Boon S, Matteelli A, Ford N, and Getahun H reviewed the continuous use of isoniazid for treating latent tuberculosis infection in people living with HIV/AIDS. Their findings were published in 2016. 16. Podany AT, Bao Y, Swindells S, Chaisson RE, Andersen JW, Mwelase T, et al. studied the pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of efavirenz in HIV-infected individuals receiving rifapentine and isoniazid for tuberculosis prevention. This research was published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2015. 17. Weiner M, Egelund EF, Engle M, Kiser M, Prihoda TJ, Gelfond JAL, et al. investigated the pharmacokinetic interaction between rifapentine and raltegravir in healthy volunteers. Their findings were published in the Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy in 2014. 18. Brooks KM, George JM, Pau AK, Rupert A, Mehaffy C, De P, et al. examined cytokine-mediated systemic adverse drug reactions in a study of dolutegravir with once-weekly isoniazid and rifapentine. This study was published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2018. 19. Dooley KE, Savic R, Gupte A, Marzinke MA, Zhang N, Edward VA, et al. conducted a phase 1/2 trial on the use of once-weekly rifapentine and isoniazid for tuberculosis prevention in patients with HIV on dolutegravir-based antiretroviral therapy. Their findings were published in The Lancet HIV in 2020. 20. WHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis prevention treatment, including a GRADE summary of evidence tables for new recommendations in 2018 and 2019, are accessible online as of September 27, 2023. 21. Guidelines on core components of infection prevention and control programs at the national and acute healthcare facility levels are available through the WHO online repository as of September 27, 2023. 22. Joshi R, Reingold AL, Menzies D, and Pai M conducted a systematic review on tuberculosis among healthcare workers in lowand middle-income countries. Their findings were published in PLoS Medicine in 2006. 23. Altice FL, Azbel L, Stone J, Brooks-Pollock E, Smyrnov P, Dvoriak S, et al. described the high-risk environment of incarceration perpetuating the transmission of HIV, hepatitis C virus, and tuberculosis in Eastern Europe and Central Asia. This study was published in The Lancet in 2016. 24. Dhavan P, Dias HM, Cresswell J, and Weil D provided an overview of tuberculosis and migration, published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2017. 25. WHO operational handbook on tuberculosis, Module 1, focuses on prevention, infection prevention, and control. It is accessible online as of September 27, 2023. 26. Srikantiah P, Lin R, Walusimbi M, Okwera A, Luzze H, Whalen CC, et al. reported elevated HIV seroprevalence and risk behavior among Ugandan TB suspects, with implications for HIV testing and prevention. This study was published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2007. 27. Odhiambo J, Kizito W, Njoroge A, Wambua N, Nganga L, Mburu M, et al. evaluated provider-initiated HIV testing and counseling for TB patients and suspects in Nairobi, Kenya. Their findings were published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2008. 28. Nliwasa M, MacPherson P, Gupta-Wright A, Mwapasa M, Horton K, Odland J, et al. conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis on the high prevalence of HIV and active tuberculosis and the increased mortality risk in adults with TB symptoms. This study was published in the Journal of the International AIDS Society in 2018. 29. WHO consolidated guidelines on collaborative TB and HIV services within a comprehensive care package for people who inject drugs are accessible online as of September 27, 2023. 30. Waldrop G, Doherty M, Vitoria M, and Ford N provided consensus definitions for stable patients and those with advanced disease to support the scale-up of antiretroviral therapy. This study was published in Tropical Medicine & International Health in 2016. 31. Egger M, May M, Chêne G, Phillips AN, Ledergerber B, Dabis F, et al. analyzed the prognosis of HIV-1-infected patients starting highly active antiretroviral therapy through a collaborative analysis of prospective studies. This study was published in The Lancet in 2002. 32. Hogg RS, Yip B, Chan KJ, Wood E, Craib KJ, O’Shaughnessy MV, et al. examined rates of disease progression by baseline CD4 cell count and viral load after initiating triple-drug therapy. This study was published in JAMA in 2001. 33. Walker AS, Prendergast AJ, Mugyenyi P, Munderi P, Hakim J, Kekitiinwa A, et al. investigated mortality in the year following antiretroviral therapy initiation in HIV-infected adults and children in Uganda and Zimbabwe. This study was published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2012. 34. Krentz HB, Auld MC, and Gill MJ analyzed the high cost of medical care for patients presenting late with HIV infection (CD4 < 200 cells/μL). This study was published in HIV Medicine in 2004. 35. Mfinanga S, Chanda D, Kivuyo SL, Guinness L, Bottomley C, Simms V, et al. conducted a randomized controlled trial on cryptococcal meningitis screening and community-based early adherence support in people with advanced HIV infection starting antiretroviral therapy in Tanzania and Zambia. This study was published in The Lancet in 2015. 36. Hakim J, Musiime V, Szubert AJ, Mallewa J, Siika A, Agutu C, et al. evaluated enhanced prophylaxis plus antiretroviral therapy for advanced HIV infection in Africa. This study was published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2017. 37. Merle C, Floyd S, Ndiaye A, Galperine T, Furco A, de Jong BC, et al. presented results from the RAFA trial, which investigated high-dose rifampicin tuberculosis treatment regimens to reduce 12-month mortality in TB/HIV co-infected patients. This study was presented at the 21st International AIDS Conference in Durban, South Africa, in 2016. 38. Amogne W, Aderaye G, Habtewold A, Yimer G, Makonnen E, Worku A, et al. conducted a randomized clinical trial on the efficacy and safety of antiretroviral therapy initiated one week after tuberculosis therapy in patients with CD4 counts < 200 cells/μL. This study was published in PLoS One in 2015. 39. WHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis, Module 6, address tuberculosis and comorbidities. These guidelines are available online as of September 27, 2023. 40. Shao HJ, Crump JA, Ramadhani HO, Uiso LO, Ole-Nguyaine S, Moon AM, et al. compared early versus delayed fixed-dose combination antiretroviral therapy in patients with HIV and tuberculosis in Tanzania. This study was published in AIDS Research and Human Retroviruses in 2009. 41. Blanc F-X, Sok T, Laureillard D, Borand L, Rekacewicz C, Nerrienet E, et al. investigated the timing of antiretroviral therapy initiation in HIV-infected adults with tuberculosis. This study was published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2011. 42. Dooley KE, Kaplan R, Mwelase N, Grinsztejn B, Ticona E, Lacerda M, et al. conducted a multicenter, non-comparative, open-label, randomized trial on dolutegravir-based antiretroviral therapy for patients co-infected with tuberculosis and HIV. This study was published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2020. 43. Kanters S, Vitoria M, Zoratti M, Doherty M, Penazzato M, Rangaraj A, et al. performed a systematic literature review and network meta-analysis comparing the efficacy, tolerability, and safety of dolutegravir and efavirenz 400 mg among antiretroviral therapies for first-line HIV treatment. This study was published in EClinicalMedicine in 2020. 44. Jamal L, Guibu I, Tancredi M, Ramalho M, Vasconcelos G, Cota I, et al. assessed the reliability and usefulness of TB/HIV co-infection data from developing countries. This study was presented at the XV International AIDS Conference in Bangkok, Thailand, in 2004. 45. Varma JK, Nateniyom S, Akksilp S, Mankatittham W, Sirinak C, Sattayawuthipong W, et al. conducted an observational study on HIV care and treatment factors associated with improved survival during TB treatment in Thailand. This study was published in BMC Infectious Diseases in 2009. 46. Shean KP, Willcox PA, Siwendu SN, Laserson KF, Gross L, Kammerer S, et al. evaluated treatment outcomes and follow-up of multidrug-resistant tuberculosis patients in South Africa from 1992 to 2002. This study was published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2008. 47. Palmero D, Ritacco V, Ambroggi M, Poggi S, Güemes Gurtubay J, Alberti F, et al. analyzed multidrug-resistant tuberculosis in AIDS patients at the beginning of the millennium. This study was published in Medicina in 2006. 48. Migliori GB, Besozzi G, Girardi E, Kliiman K, Lange C, Toungoussova OS, et al. assessed the clinical and operational value of the extensively drug-resistant tuberculosis definition. This study was published in the European Respiratory Journal in 2007. 49. Leimane V, Dravniece G, Riekstina V, Sture I, Kammerer S, Chen MP, et al. evaluated treatment outcomes of multidrug/extensively drug-resistant tuberculosis in Latvia from 2000 to 2004. This study was published in the European Respiratory Journal in 2010. 50. El Sahly HM, Teeter LD, Pawlak RR, Musser JM, Graviss EA analyzed drug-resistant tuberculosis as a disease of target populations in Houston, Texas. This study was published in the Journal of Infectious Diseases in 2006. 51. Eker B, Ortmann J, Migliori GB, Sotgiu G, Muetterlein R, Centis R, et al. investigated multidrugand extensively drug-resistant tuberculosis in Germany. This study was published in Emerging Infectious Diseases in 2008. 52. Dheda K, Shean K, Zumla A, Badri M, Streicher EM, Page-Shipp L, et al. conducted a retrospective cohort study on early treatment outcomes and HIV status of patients with extensively drug-resistant tuberculosis in South Africa. This study was published in The Lancet in 2010. 53. Burgos M, Gonzalez LC, Paz EA, Gournis E, Kawamura LM, Schecter G, et al. evaluated an outpatient-based approach for treating multidrug-resistant tuberculosis in San Francisco. This study was published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2005. 54. Nunn AJ, Mwaba P, Chintu C, Mwinga A, Darbyshire JH, Zumla A, et al. conducted a randomized clinical trial on the role of co-trimoxazole prophylaxis in reducing mortality in HIV-infected adults being treated for tuberculosis. This study was published in BMJ in 2008. 55. Wiktor SZ, Sassan-Morokro M, Grant AD, Abouya L, Karon JM, Maurice C, et al. evaluated the efficacy of trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole prophylaxis in reducing morbidity and mortality in HIV-1-infected patients with tuberculosis in Côte d’Ivoire. This study was published in The Lancet in 1999. 56. Zachariah R, Spielmann MP, Harries AD, Salaniponi FL investigated voluntary counseling, HIV testing, and sexual behavior among tuberculosis patients in rural Malawi. This study was published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2003. 57. Chimzizi RB, Harries AD, Manda E, Khonyongwa A, Salaniponi FM evaluated the implementation of counseling, HIV testing, and adjunctive co-trimoxazole for TB patients in Malawi. This study was published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2004. 58. Mwaungulu FBD, Floyd S, Crampin AC, Kasimba S, Malema S, Kanyongoloka H, et al. demonstrated that co-trimoxazole prophylaxis reduces mortality in HIV-positive tuberculosis patients in Malawi. This study was published in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization in 2004. 59. Legido-Quigley H, Montgomery CM, Khan P, Atun R, Fakoya A, Getahun H, et al. conducted a systematic review on integrating tuberculosis and HIV services in lowand middle-income countries. This study was published in Tropical Medicine & International Health in 2013. 60. WHO released a policy brief on the role of HIV viral suppression in improving individual health and reducing transmission. This document is accessible online as of September 28, 2023. 61. Gupta A, Bhosale R, Kinikar A, Gupte N, Bharadwaj R, Kagal A, et al. identified maternal tuberculosis as a risk factor for mother-to-child transmission of HIV. This study was published in the Journal of Infectious Diseases in 2011. 62. WHO published a summary on the safe management of healthcare waste, accessible online as of September 28, 2023. 63. Gunneberg C, Reid A, Williams BG, Floyd K, Nunn P reviewed global monitoring of collaborative TB-HIV activities. This study was published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2008. 64. Martinot A, Van Rie A, Mulangu S, Mbulula M, Jarrett N, Behets F, et al. conducted a baseline assessment of collaborative TB/HIV activities in Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of Congo. This study was published in Tropical Doctor in 2008. 65. WHO released consolidated HIV strategic information guidelines to drive impact through program monitoring and management. This document is accessible online as of September 28, 2023. 66. WHO published a guide to monitoring and evaluation for collaborative TB/HIV activities, revised in 2015. This document is accessible online as of September 28, 2023. 67. WHO outlined priority research questions for TB/HIV in HIV-prevalent and resource-limited settings. This document is accessible online as of September 28, 2023.
